subject: VAT ledger mapping discrepancy for CloudOptix Q2 invoices
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 08:14:00 +0000
Subject: VAT ledger mapping discrepancy for CloudOptix Q2 invoices

Marcus / Neha —

I pulled the AR aging for CloudOptix and noticed a VAT mismatch affecting five invoices in May–June. The amounts collected include VAT charged at the customer country rate, but the revenue side in NetSuite has been mapped to our generic SaaS revenue account instead of the VAT-included revenue buckets we use for EU customers. That mismatch is causing two issues: (1) AR balances don't roll to the expected GL accounts and (2) deferred revenue mapping for a recognition batch next week will be off.

Quick summary: attached CSV (7462-CloudOptix-InvoiceSummary-Q2.csv) shows invoice numbers, issued dates, VAT rate applied, and current GL mapping from NetSuite. Example problem: Invoice 2026-7543 shows VAT 20% collected but revenue posted to 4000-SaaS-Service (no VAT bucket), whereas in prior quarters EU invoices post to 4012-SaaS-EU-VAT.

Can finance confirm whether we should:
- post retrospective journal corrections to move revenue into VAT-aware revenue accounts (JE template attached), and
- book a VAT liability adjustment if the tax mapping was inconsistent?

Neha — can you take a look and propose the journal entries (NS JE format) and whether we need to adjust any customer statements before we collect outstanding amounts?

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Sr. Accounting Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 7462-CloudOptix-InvoiceSummary-Q2.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: VAT ledger mapping discrepancy for CloudOptix Q2 invoices

Thanks Laura — good catch. Mikael, apologies for the interruption — we're doing an internal clean-up of a mapping issue that may affect the customer-facing AR statements for a handful of invoices from Q2. No action required from CloudOptix yet; we'll confirm before any statements are reissued.

Neha — please take lead. If we need to issue adjusted statements I'd like to get sign-off from legal/tax counsel before sending. I’m looping in Stephanie because we may need a short customer note templates and Logan (cc removed for brevity) for communications.

Target timeline: outline proposed JE by end of day tomorrow (Fri 6/26), and a final runbook for posting + communication by Monday 6/29.

Marcus Lin
Director, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 15:48:00 +0000
Subject: Re: VAT ledger mapping discrepancy for CloudOptix Q2 invoices

Folks — reviewed the CSV and ran a quick NetSuite trial balance for the affected invoices. Summary below and attached a draft JE in NetSuite template (NS-JE-Proposal-20260626.xlsx).

Findings:
- 5 invoices (INV-2026-7498, 7543, 7610, 7691, 7745) were billed to EU addresses but revenue posted to 4000-SaaS-Service. VAT was captured to 2200-VAT-Received as expected at collection, but our revenue recognition mapping didn't allocate to the EU-revenue sub-accounts.
- Total gross reclassification required: EUR 112,540 (net EUR 93,783 + VAT EUR 18,757).

Proposal (high level):
1) Create reversing JE to move gross amounts from 4000-SaaS-Service to a temporary clearing account (9999-REV-CLEARING).
2) Post reclassification JE: debit 9999-REV-CLEARING credit 4012-SaaS-EU-VAT (net) and move VAT portion to 2201-VAT-Liability-EU if needed.
3) Add memo lines tying back to original invoice numbers and HubSpot record 404512.

Compliance check: I recommend we loop in external VAT counsel to confirm the VAT liability treatment if any of the invoices were cross-border B2B with valid reverse-charge indicators.

Next steps I can take if approved: finalize NS JE file, schedule JE for weekday close window (Tue 6/30), and prepare a customer-facing note for CloudOptix if we must reissue statements.

Attachments: NS-JE-Proposal-20260626.xlsx

Neha Kapoor
Accounting Manager, Revenue
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: VAT ledger mapping discrepancy for CloudOptix Q2 invoices

Neha — this approach looks sound. Elena — can you confirm whether the VAT liability should stay in 2200-VAT-Received or be reclassified to 2201-VAT-Liability-EU when we move revenue to the EU-specific revenue account? Also: if any of these were B2B reverse-charge, is a retrospective liability adjustment required?

Mikael — we'll only reissue statements if we need to correct the invoice tax lines; otherwise this will be an internal reclassification and your AR balance will not change. I'll flag here before we do anything customer-facing.

Thanks all,
Marcus
From: Elena Rossi <elena@acctadvisors.eu>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2026 16:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: VAT ledger mapping discrepancy for CloudOptix Q2 invoices

Quick note after a brief review — based on the invoice samples you sent, these look like standard B2C-style VAT charges (customer countries indicated and VAT shown on invoice). Two key points: (1) VAT collected should remain in a liability account (2201-VAT-Liability-EU) and can be reclassified from 2200 if your chart uses separate buckets; (2) if any invoices were actually correctly marked as B2B with valid VAT numbers, those would be reverse-charge and should not have VAT recorded — that would require a corrective invoice and potential VAT credit.

Recommendation: proceed with Neha's JE plan but add an additional verification step: validate customer VAT registration status for the five invoices (HubSpot 404512 has the business contact). If any are B2B with valid VAT IDs, prepare corrective credit notes before posting JEs.

I can review the finalized JE file Monday morning CET if you upload the spreadsheet to the secure advice link (or share via the NetSuite attachment).

Elena Rossi
Senior VAT Advisor
AccountAdvisors EU

Attachments: VAT-lookup-notes.pdf
